content: {"id": "7be829ea-119c-47cb-8767-edeb991fafce", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "We moved our application from us-east-1 to eu-west-1 but kept calling Bedrock in us-east-1. Our client measured p50 per Converse call at about 1.2 s before the move and about 1.6 s after; our agent makes 6 sequential model calls per user request, and nothing else changed. Why is it slower and what should we do?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "c48b02f1-b33c-4b04-b8ce-a79eceb414da", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Latency increase after moving app to eu-west-1"}]}

{"id": "97d1c96f-02d0-4cad-9c90-4d92d044bb7a", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Cross-region latency between eu-west-1 and us-east-1 explains part of the delay, but 400ms per call is more than a single RTT would account for. That gap likely comes from TLS handshake overhead on new connections—if the connection isn't reused, TCP plus TLS 1.3 plus the actual request adds up to roughly three round trips—and possibly differences in streaming versus non-streaming behavior.

This is really about Bedrock's cross-region inference setup, so a good fix would be calling Bedrock directly in eu-west-1 using the EU cross-region inference profile to keep traffic within the region. I'll answer directly without verifying further, being clear I haven't measured this myself, and keep the explanation concise.

boto3 pools connections automatically, so I'd also reduce sequential calls with prompt caching, streaming for faster first-token, trimming context, and parallelizing independent calls—plus flagging the EU-to-US data residency concern. I should also note Bedrock's Converse response includes server-side metrics.latencyMs, so subtracting that from client-measured p50 isolates network overhead; I'd expect server-side latency to stay roughly constant around 1.2s.

"}]}

{"id": "01828fb3-f7f9-478e-8ed2-0416f043ae1b", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**The slowdown is most likely network distance.** Your app now sits about 70 to 90 ms round-trip from the Bedrock endpoint it calls (eu-west-1 to us-east-1). I haven't measured your setup, so treat the details below as the likely explanation.

**Why the delta is about 400 ms**

- Model inference time shouldn't change, because the model still runs in us-east-1.
- A single round trip only accounts for about 80 ms. About 400 ms is closer to 4 or 5 round trips, so more is going on than one hop.
- If connections aren't being reused, each call pays a new TCP and TLS handshake, which is 2 to 3 round trips before the request is sent.
- Large prompts (long context, tool results, images) need several round trips to upload, because TCP's congestion window starts small. Before the move those round trips cost almost nothing, and now each one costs about 80 ms.
- With 6 sequential calls, the extra cost compounds to about 2.4 s per user request.

**What to do**

1. **Call Bedrock in eu-west-1.** This is the real fix, because it removes the transatlantic hop.
   - Check that your model is available there. If it isn't available on-demand, use an EU cross-region inference profile (model IDs prefixed `eu.`). That keeps inference inside EU regions, and it also helps with throughput.
   - If you had a reason to keep calling us-east-1, such as model availability, check data residency too. Prompts and responses are currently crossing the Atlantic.
2. **Confirm connections are being reused.** Create one Bedrock runtime client at startup and reuse it. Don't build a client per call or per request. Check that keep-alive and connection pooling are on in your HTTP client. This matters most if you stay cross-region.
3. **Confirm where the time goes.** Compare your client-side latency with `metrics.latencyMs` in the Converse response, which is the server-side time.
   - If server-side time is still about 1.2 s, the extra 0.4 s is network and connection overhead. That confirms the diagnosis.
   - If server-side time also rose, something else is going on and we should look further.
4. **Cut the cost of the 6 sequential calls:**
   - Use prompt caching for the static system prompt and tool definitions, which shrinks the payload and cuts model time.
   - Trim the context carried between calls.
   - Run independent steps in parallel.
   - Stream responses (`ConverseStream`) so users see output sooner, even if total time doesn't change.
   - For supported models, try the latency-optimized inference setting.

If you can share the model ID and your typical prompt size, I can help work out whether an EU inference profile fits your case.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
